'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***Large clashes with [[Airstrike|air raids]] and [[artillery]] in the Ombada district in northern [[Khartoum]] leave over 16 people dead, including 2 confirmed children. [https://globeecho.com/news/africa/sudan-air-raids-and-artillery-fire-in-khartoum-at-least-16-civilians-killed/ (Globe Echo)]
**[[Battle of Omdurman (2023)|Battle of Omdurman]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] shells three [[Rapid Support Forces|RSF]]-held neighbourhoods in [[Omdurman]], [[Khartoum (state)|Khartoum State]], [[Sudan]], killing at least 18 people and injuring dozens more. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/25/sudan-city-omdurman-attack (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Russia–United States relations]]
***The [[United States Central Command]] says that a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian military]] jet damaged an [[General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper|MQ-9 Reaper]] drone in [[Syria]]n airspace on July 23, by ejecting [[flare (countermeasure)|flares]] while flying "dangerously close" to the U.S. aircraft. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-66306030 (BBC News)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Three [[Hamas]] members are killed by [[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] in the [[Nablus]] neighborhood of al-Tur, in the occupied [[West Bank]]. [https://apnews.com/article/palestinian-militants-israel-army-west-bank-attack-raid-893c2f08314f08a2116b4a1751ce7850 (AP)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***The United States announces a $400 million military aid package to Ukraine. The package includes various anti-tank and air defense missiles, 32 [[Stryker]] armored fighting vehicles, [[Hydra 70]] rockets, and [[Black Hornet Nano]] surveillance [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|drones]], among other equipment. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2023/jul/25/russia-ukraine-war-live-moscow-drone-strike-kyiv-un-mines-zaporizhzhia-plant?page=with:block-64c022648f082e4442451f69#block-64c022648f082e4442451f69 (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in 2023]]
**[[2023 Italy wildfires]]
***Four people are killed by [[wildfire]]s in [[southern Italy]]. A firefighter also dies in [[Sardinia]] while fighting fires in [[Baunei]]. [https://www.repubblica.it/cronaca/2023/07/25/diretta/maltempo_incendi_italia_oggi-408911952/#408911952_event13 (''La Repubblica'')]
**[[2023 Greece wildfires]]
***Two [[Hellenic Air Force|air force]] members are killed when a [[Canadair CL-215]] [[Aerial firefighting|waterbomber]] crashes on [[Euboea|Evia island]], [[Greece]]. [https://metro.co.uk/2023/07/25/greece-wildfires-plane-crash-evia-19188820/?ico=metro-posts_article_whats-trending-now (''Metro'')]
*Four people are killed and several others are injured by [[flood]]s in [[Lombardy]], [[Italy]]. Heavy rains also occur in [[Veneto]]. [https://www.fanpage.it/milano/live/maltempo-oggi-a-milano-violento-temporale-durante-la-notte-molti-i-danni-in-tutta-la-lombardia/ (''Fanpage'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*Fifty-one [[long-finned pilot whale]]s are found dead after [[Cetacean stranding|beaching]] themselves on a beach near [[Albany, Western Australia|Albany]], [[Western Australia]], as part of a larger pod of nearly 100. State authorities and volunteers are working to redirect the remaining 46 whales to deeper waters. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/pilot-whales-dead-beaching-western-australia-albany-perth-3654531 (AFP via CNA)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2023 Quran desecration in Sweden]]
**[[Denmark–Egypt relations]], [[Denmark–Turkey relations]]
***[[Far-right politics|Far-right]] protesters [[book burning|set fire]] to copies of the [[Quran]] outside the [[Egypt]]ian and [[Turkey|Turkish]] embassies in [[Copenhagen]], [[Denmark]], prompting outrage from [[Muslim world|Muslim-majority]] countries. [https://www.politico.eu/article/far-right-group-burn-quran-copenhagen-denmark/ (''Politico'')]
**[[Foreign relations of Egypt]], [[Foreign relations of Sweden]]
*** The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Egypt)|Egyptian foreign ministry]] summons [[Sweden]]'s envoy over protests in [[Stockholm]] that desecrated the Quran. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2023/07/25/Egypt-summons-Swedish-envoy-over-Quran-protests (AFP via Al Arabiya)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Islamic terrorism in Europe]]
**Six men are found guilty of [[terrorist]] [[murder]] for their participation in the [[2016 Brussels bombings|Brussels bombings in 2016]], with two of them also being found guilty for their roles in the [[November 2015 Paris attacks|Paris attacks in 2015]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-66299186 (BBC News)]
*[[Ecuadorian security crisis]]
**[[Ecuador]] declares a [[state of emergency]] in all prisons after [[July 2023 Guayaquil prison riot|gang clashes that killed 31 prisoners]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/25/ecuador-prison-state-of-emergency-hostages-killings (''The Guardian'')]
*A 25-year-old man is [[criminal charge|charged]] with three counts of [[murder]], including one as a [[Domestic violence in Australia|domestic violence]] offense, four days after intentionally causing a fatal accident that killed three people on the [[Bruce Highway]] in [[Federal, Queensland]], [[Australia]]. The suspected killer had been chasing one of the vehicles prior to the accident. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-07-25/man-charged-with-murder-after-triple-fatal-bruce-highway-crash/102642668 (ABC News Australia)]
*A five-month-old girl dies when [[Law enforcement in India|Indian forces]] fire [[tear gas]] at [[Rohingya refugees in India|Rohingya refugees]] trying to escape a [[Immigration detention|detention centre]] in [[Hiranagar]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2023/jul/25/baby-dies-after-teargas-fired-rohingya-refugees--try-escape-indian-detention-jammu-kashmir (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[United States Department of Education]] initiates a civil rights investigation into [[Harvard University]]'s [[Legacy preferences|legacy admissions]] policy, in accordance with the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] ruling ''[[Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard]]''. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/07/27/world/americas-emea/us-probe-opened-on-harvards-legacy-admissions-policy/1902588 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[2023 Carolina, Puerto Rico massacre|One man and two teenaged boys]] from [[Guayama, Puerto Rico]] are found dead in the northern city of [[Carolina, Puerto Rico|Carolina]]. Hours earlier, two Guayama teenaged girls, aged 13 and 15, had also been found dead inside a Toyota Tacoma vehicle near [[Luis Munoz Marin International Airport]], also in Carolina. Authorities confirmed their belief that the crimes are related. [https://www.telemundopr.com/noticias/puerto-rico/confirman-vinculo-entre-masacre-en-carolina-y-adolescentes-asesinadas-en-pinones/2511411/ (Telemundo)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Capital punishment in Ghana]]
**The [[Parliament of Ghana]] votes to formally abolish the [[capital punishment|death penalty]], becoming the latest African nation to end the punishment. The 176 prisoners currently on [[death row]] in Ghanian prisons will now have their sentences changed to [[life imprisonment]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-66308724 (BBC News)]
*[[2024 United States presidential election]]
**The [[Ron DeSantis 2024 presidential campaign|presidential campaign]] of [[Governor of Florida|Florida Governor]] [[Ron DeSantis]] fires former ''[[National Review]]'' writer Nate Hochman for posting videos that include [[Anti-LGBT rhetoric|anti-LGBT]] and [[Neo-Nazism|neo-Nazi]] content. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/jul/26/desantis-campaign-video-nazi-symbol-fired-aide (''The Guardian'')]
*[[China|Chinese]] state media announces that [[Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|Foreign Minister]] [[Qin Gang]] has been replaced by his predecessor [[Wang Yi (politician)|Wang Yi]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/7/25/wang-yi-replaces-qin-gang-as-chinese-foreign-minister-what-to-know (Al Jazeera)]

**[[Casey Phair]], participating as part of the [[South Korea women's national football team|South Korean football team]] in a match against [[Colombia women's national football team|Colombia]], becomes the youngest player to appear at a [[FIFA Women's World Cup]] game at 16 years old. [https://www.npr.org/2023/07/25/1189899320/an-american-becomes-the-youngest-to-debut-in-the-womens-world-cup-for-south-kore (NPR)]
**The [[BBC World Service|BBC]] apologises for asking [[Morocco women's national football team|Morocco]] captain [[Ghizlane Chebbak]] how many of the team are [[Homosexuality in association football|lesbians]].
